subject: psychiatry
title: Specific Learning Disorders and Childhood Communication Deficits

steps.tx: **Specific learning disorder**, abbreviated SLD, is diagnosed when a child exhibits persistent difficulties learning and using academic skills despite targeted interventions for at least six months. Affected academic performance lies substantially below developmental expectations on individualized standardized achievement testing, in the setting of normal intellect.
steps.say: Specific learning disorder involves academic achievement substantially below cognitive capability, persisting for six months despite targeted remedial help.

vis.title: Specific Learning Disorder Subtypes
rows: Phonological decoding & sight word recognition failure
Orthographic spelling, syntax, and spatial letter formation
Number sense, mathematical calculation, & arithmetic facts

steps.tx: **Developmental dyslexia** represents the most prevalent specific learning disorder, accounting for approximately 80 percent of all SLD diagnoses. Sufferers exhibit core deficits in phonological processing, struggling to map graphemes to phonemes, which manifests as inaccurate, effortful, slow reading, frequent letter reversals (such as confusing 'b' and 'd'), and poor comprehension.
steps.say: Dyslexia accounts for eighty percent of learning disorders, driven by phonological deficits causing slow, inaccurate reading and letter reversals.

left.title: Reading Deficits
points: Poor reading comprehension of written passages

right.title: Preserved Cognitive Faculties
points: Intact logical reasoning and problem solving

steps.tx: Study the errors scattered through this child's written work, where letters turn backward and words are spelled as they sound. Such **phonological spelling errors**, with reversals of letters like b and d, are typical classroom evidence in dyslexia and dysgraphia. A single sample never makes the diagnosis, but work like this should trigger formal assessment of reading accuracy, fluency, spelling, and handwriting speed.
steps.say: Reversed letters and sound-based spellings in this sample are typical of dyslexia and dysgraphia. They should prompt formal testing of reading and writing skills.

steps.tx: **Neurobiological circuitry in dyslexia** reveals functional hypoactivation within left hemisphere posterior reading networks, specifically the left parieto-temporal junction (phonological decoding) and left occipito-temporal word-form area (automatic sight-word reading). Compensatory hyperactivation occurs in the right hemisphere and anterior left inferior frontal gyrus (Broca area).
steps.say: Dyslexia involves hypoactivation in the left occipito-temporal and parieto-temporal reading centers, with compensatory frontal activation.

nodes.label: Visual input received in primary occipital striate cortex
Left occipito-temporal visual word-form area (hypoactive in dyslexia)
Left parieto-temporal phonological decoding center (hypoactive in dyslexia)
Compensatory recruitment of left Broca area & right hemisphere homologs

steps.tx: **Dyscalculia** involves specific impairments in mathematical cognition, affecting the comprehension of number concepts, numerical facts, arithmetic symbols, and computational execution. Children struggle to determine which number is larger, rely persistently on immature finger counting long after peers, and cannot align multi-digit addition columns.
steps.say: Dyscalculia impairs number sense, arithmetic calculation, and numerical reasoning, often seen as persistent finger counting and calculation errors.

vis.title: Dyscalculia Clinical Features
rows: Inability to estimate quantities or compare numbers
Left angular gyrus and hippocampal encoding
Errors in multi-step carrying and borrowing
Misaligning vertical columns in long division

steps.tx: **Dysgraphia** involves impaired written expression manifesting as poor spatial letter formation, irregular spacing, grammatical inaccuracies, and severe spelling errors. Children exhibit an awkward pencil grip, fatigue rapidly during handwriting tasks, and display a marked discrepancy between articulate spoken language and impoverished written essays.
steps.say: Dysgraphia causes illegible handwriting, awkward pencil grip, and spelling errors, with spoken ability far exceeding written output.

left.title: Motor & Spatial Dysgraphia
points: Failure to adhere to ruled page margins
Excessive time spent forming individual letters

right.title: Orthographic Dysgraphia
points: Struggles to organize thoughts into paragraphs
Intact verbal story narration when spoken

steps.tx: **Childhood-onset fluency disorder**, commonly known as stuttering or stammering, is a communication disorder characterized by frequent, marked prolongations, sound repetitions, and broken words (pauses within words). Physical tension and involuntary motor grimaces often accompany speech blocks, characteristically disappearing when the individual sings or whispers.
steps.say: Stuttering involves sound repetitions, syllable prolongations, and speech blocks, which characteristically disappear when singing or speaking to animals.

vis.title: Fluency Disturbance Spectrum
rows: Tense silent pause with lip struggle
Inability to initiate vocal cord vibration
Bypasses left hemisphere; activates right auditory cortex

steps.tx: **Social pragmatic communication disorder** involves persistent difficulties in the social use of verbal and non-verbal communication, such as greeting, sharing information, and adapting communication to match the context. Sufferers fail to understand non-literal language, metaphors, irony, and humor, yet strictly lack the restricted, repetitive behaviors required for autism.
steps.say: Social pragmatic communication disorder impairs conversational rules and understanding of humor and idioms, without the repetitive rituals of autism.

right.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder
points: Inflexible adherence to rigid daily routines

steps.tx: **Multisensory remedial education** constitutes the definitive evidence-based intervention for specific learning disorders, utilizing structured, sequential phonics programs like the Orton-Gillingham approach. Accommodations such as extended examination time, oral examinations, text-to-speech software, and calculators allow students to demonstrate mastery without penalty.
steps.say: Remedial education uses structured multisensory phonics like the Orton-Gillingham method, supported by extended exam time and assistive technology.

nodes.label: Formal psychoeducational assessment establishing IQ-achievement disparity
School accommodations: 25-50% extended exam time & reader assistance
Assistive software: speech-to-text dictation and digital calculators
